primitives.name: Physiological Load State
primitives.verbatim_quote: Nobody in the market prices **fatigue, recovery state, or cumulative physiological load as a continuous latent variable** — and this paper demonstrates the underlying quantity is real and state-dependent.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Dimensionless state variable $L \in [0,1]$, with higher values indicating greater accumulated fatigue/cumulative load.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that physiological load is additive and Markovian; assumes that proxies are informative about the true latent state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when load accumulates non-linearly or when proxies become uncorrelated with the true state.

layer2.mapping: Models the latent state as a hidden Markov process observed through noisy proxy features, used to adjust prop projections.
layer2.telemetry: Historical backtest showing improvement in prop projection RMSE after incorporating the estimated state variable.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core failure mode of the original paper is its reliance on a high-frequency radar system with severe limitations (n=15, no ground truth). However, the key insight—that exertion alters physiological state and can be classified—survives. This becomes a new signal class for props, where continuous latent variables (fatigue, load) are currently unpriced. The Wavelet Scattering Transform (WST) serves as a cheap spike test, revealing that high accuracy on standard CV masks poor generalization (LOSO). This motivates a validation discipline using random-CV versus leave-one-subject-out gaps. Scale-source decomposition isolates where model power originates, preventing over-reliance on team-level features. Together, these primitives enable GSE to build unpriced physiological-load signals without requiring proprietary hardware.
